trust_decision.summary: Which column identifiers go into the DELETE ... WHERE clause for a permission link: at the pinned commit the raw JSON map keys supplied by the client (any number of them) are concatenated as SQL identifiers in DatabaseStorage.removePermission; the fix derives the two identifiers from the resolved model classes and rejects maps that do not have exactly two entries.

landing_point.why: The summary names DELETE /api/permissions; the JAX-RS resource that binds that route is the first place to look, and it leads one call down to DatabaseStorage.removePermission.

fix_sites.module_kind: storage layer (SQL query builder for the database backend)

fix_sites.entry_point: Permission(LinkedHashMap) constructor: called from POST/DELETE /api/permissions[/bulk] (PermissionsResource.java:95,121) and from the DB read path QueryBuilder.executePermissionsQuery (QueryBuilder.java:360)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Permission.java:54 constructor check is a shared model; it is the obvious validation point for the resource, not an out-of-scope module. The only other implementation, MemoryStorage.removePermission (src/main/java/org/traccar/storage/MemoryStorage.java:179-182), uses resolved classes/ids and builds no SQL.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No uncovered route found; the only argument available is that addPermission (DatabaseStorage.java:212-227) uses map keys too, but it binds values only and never puts keys into SQL, so it is correctly not a sink.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate permission keys are resolved case-insensitively and include prefixed model names (e.g. managedUserId, which maps to table tc_user_user via prefix stripping); an over-broad key whitelist or exact-case match would break linking managed users or case-variant clients. The same constructor also rebuilds Permission objects from SELECT * results on the read path, so a check that rejects DB column labels would break GET /api/permissions.

O6_input_shapes: extra (third and later) map keys appended to the WHERE clause (DatabaseStorage.java:235; closed by fix.diff:24-26)

first two keys whose last two characters are arbitrary: getKeyClass strips two chars and looks up case-insensitively, so the raw key text differs from the resolved identity (Permission.java:35,77-79; closed by fix.diff:43-44)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: addPermission building an explicit column list 'INSERT INTO t (k1, k2) VALUES (?, ?)' from permission.get() keys
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Positional VALUES depends on map order matching column order; a maintainer making the insert order-independent would naturally list the entry keys as columns, reusing the same pattern removePermission uses.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: getPermissions taking the raw query-parameter keys from GET /api/permissions (PermissionsResource.java:79-85) as condition columns instead of Permission.getKey(class)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The resource already filters raw keys by endsWith("Id") and passes them around; passing the key string through to the storage layer is a plausible shortcut.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: formatPermissionQuery deriving outputKey/conditionKey from a caller-supplied key string
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same identifier-in-SQL position as the fixed site, inside a builder deep in the storage layer the resource never calls directly.

O9_family: SQL injection (identifier position: column names from client JSON keys) / CWE-89

services: embedded H2 database usable (build.gradle:88); no external services required
O10_build.project_tests: No tests for PermissionsResource or DatabaseStorage permissions; only src/test/java/org/traccar/storage/QueryBuilderTest.java exists in the storage test package.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Only reject maps with more than two entries (or truncate to the first two), leaving the raw first two key strings, whose last two characters are never checked, concatenated into the DELETE clause.

out_of_scope_notes: ORDER BY column (DatabaseStorage.java:371-375) is fed by sortField, but sortField is a constructor constant (ExtendedObjectResource.java:40-42,83; SimpleObjectResource.java:39-41,72), not user input; not pursued.
GET /api/permissions (PermissionsResource.java:79-85) can pass a null class from getKeyClass for unknown keys; robustness issue, not this sink.

Whether the two-character suffix differential on the first two keys is exploitable on its own (beyond producing SQL errors) was not assessed.
